identity.name: Blinder Tunnel (CL-STA-1178) — Developer-Lure MSBuild Execution, GitHub-as-C2 and Chisel Tunnel (T1127 / T1574.014 / T1102.002 / T1572)
identity.summary: A fake Dubai Airports coding test runs a GetFrameworkPaths MSBuild target when opened, drops a renamed RuntimeBroker.exe with an ETW-disabling AppDomainManager config, persists as MicrosoftRuntime, uses GitHub as C2 and tunnels via Blackwood/Chisel. Endpoint and network alerts stitch on one host; the GitHub relay is seen at the network boundary (no SaaS-audit emitter yet).
identity.description: Unit 42 attributes Blinder Tunnel to CL-STA-1178, an Iran-nexus cluster targeting Iraqi critical infrastructure. The victim is approached as a job candidate, completes a fake Dubai Airports HR questionnaire, then receives DubaiAirport_Carrers_IT_Test.zip: a Visual Studio project with a deliberate loop bug. FlightManager.csproj defines a GetFrameworkPaths target that Visual Studio runs during its design-time build, so opening the project — not compiling it — creates %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\RuntimeBrokers, copies binaries there and launches a signed vshost.exe renamed RuntimeBroker.exe. RuntimeBroker.exe.config hijacks the AppDomainManager to load ShelbyLoader V2 (RuntimeBroker.dll) and sets etwEnable to false; PsProxy.dll runs PowerShell in-process without powershell.exe. Persistence is an HKCU Run value named MicrosoftRuntime. C2 is a GitHub repository (peakyblinders-tm/myLic) driven through the contents API with a hard-coded token: the implant uploads a Base64 fingerprint to <machineId>/Lic.txt and polls <machineId>/Inf.txt every 63 seconds, falling back to the Issues search API when the token is revoked. Blackwood wraps Chisel to build a reverse SOCKS tunnel (R:0.0.0.0:10999:socks) to 91.107.156.29. SIM-MP-025 reproduces the endpoint lineage for real (renamed benign binaries, real config files, real autostart entry, the GitHub URI shape sent to a lab stage host), emits the GitHub cadence and the tunnel / WildFire records as shape-true NGFW logs carrying the run host's identity, and resolves the report's phishing domains through a named lab resolver. The GitHub SaaS relay is observed at the network boundary (NGFW App-ID), not through a SaaS audit log, because no SaaS-audit emitter exists (backlog). CR-MP-0025 stitches the endpoint and network legs on src_host.

biocs.name: MP-025 Build Engine Drops and Executes RuntimeBroker from User App-Data
biocs.description: A build engine (MSBuild.exe or dotnet msbuild) running under the IDE creates Microsoft\RuntimeBrokers in the user's local app-data, copies binaries into it and launches RuntimeBroker.exe from there. A design-time target (GetFrameworkPaths) has no business installing and running a binary; this is the Blinder Tunnel T1127 execution primitive.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("MSBuild.exe", "msbuild", "dotnet", "dotnet.exe", "sh")
| filter action_process_image_path contains "Microsoft\\RuntimeBrokers" or action_process_image_path contains "Microsoft/RuntimeBrokers"
| filter action_process_image_name = "RuntimeBroker.exe"
| comp count() as launches by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_path
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_path, launches

biocs.name: MP-025 RuntimeBroker.exe Executed Outside System32
biocs.description: A process named RuntimeBroker.exe starts from a path other than \Windows\System32 — here %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\RuntimeBrokers, where the report's renamed vshost.exe lives. Masquerading as the Windows Runtime Broker.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "RuntimeBroker.exe"
| filter action_process_image_path not contains "System32"
| comp count() as starts by agent_hostname, action_process_image_path, actor_process_image_name
| fields agent_hostname, action_process_image_path, actor_process_image_name, starts

biocs.name: MP-025 AppDomainManager Config with ETW Disabled Beside User-Writable EXE
biocs.description: A .exe.config is written next to an executable in a user-writable folder and declares appDomainManagerAssembly / appDomainManagerType together with etwEnable enabled=false — the AppDomainManager hijack that loads ShelbyLoader V2 while blinding .NET ETW.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_file_name contains ".exe.config"
| filter action_file_path contains "RuntimeBrokers" or action_file_path contains "AppData"
| comp count() as config_writes by agent_hostname, action_file_path, actor_process_image_name
| fields agent_hostname, action_file_path, actor_process_image_name, config_writes

biocs.name: MP-025 MicrosoftRuntime Autostart Pointing at App-Data RuntimeBroker
biocs.description: An autostart value named MicrosoftRuntime (HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, or an XDG autostart entry on Linux) points at RuntimeBroker.exe under the user's app-data — the report's persistence value.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter (event_type = ENUM.REGISTRY and action_registry_key_name contains "CurrentVersion\\Run" and action_registry_value_name = "MicrosoftRuntime") or (event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_name = "MicrosoftRuntime.desktop")
| comp count() as autostart_writes by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, autostart_writes

biocs.name: MP-025 Lic/Inf C2 Files Written Under RuntimeBrokers
biocs.description: A non-browser, non-git process descended from the build-engine lineage writes Lic.txt or Inf.txt under Microsoft\RuntimeBrokers — the machine-fingerprint and command files the implant mirrors to the attacker's GitHub repository.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_file_name in ("Lic.txt", "Inf.txt")
| filter action_file_path contains "RuntimeBrokers"
| comp count() as c2_file_writes by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_image_name
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_image_name, c2_file_writes

biocs.name: MP-025 chisel-v3 WebSocket Upgrade from RuntimeBrokers Chain
biocs.description: A process in the RuntimeBrokers causality chain writes Blackwood.dll.conf and opens an HTTP/1.1 WebSocket upgrade advertising Sec-WebSocket-Protocol chisel-v3 — Chisel reverse-SOCKS tunnel setup from a masqueraded host.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter (event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_name = "Blackwood.dll.conf") or (event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and action_process_image_command_line contains "chisel-v3")
| comp count() as tunnel_setup_events by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, tunnel_setup_events

abiocs.name: MP-025 Recurring Fixed-Cadence GitHub API Sessions from a Non-Developer-Pattern Host
abiocs.description: A host whose GitHub usage is normally interactive (browser, git) starts a burst of small HTTPS sessions to api.github.com (an 8-session burst; the 63 s interval is the report's, not the record's) — the Blinder Tunnel GitHub contents-API C2 relay as the NGFW (App-ID) records it at the network boundary; no SaaS-audit leg exists (backlog). GitHub is legitimate, so no IOC matches; the ABIOC fires on the burst deviation for the host, anchored to endpoint_device_name so it stitches to the endpoint lineage.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter log_source_type = "eal" and url_domain = "api.github.com" and action = "allow"
| comp count() as sessions, avg(bytes_sent) as avg_bytes by endpoint_device_name, src
| filter sessions >= 6 and avg_bytes < 8192
| sort desc sessions
| fields endpoint_device_name, src, sessions, avg_bytes
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-host network-boundary usage baseline for GitHub (interactive, bursty) -> a burst of small API sessions to api.github.com from the same endpoint_device_name that runs the RuntimeBrokers lineage.

abiocs.name: MP-025 Recurring Tunnel Sessions to a Rare IP-Literal Destination
abiocs.description: The run host holds a recurring series of sessions to a destination reached by IP literal and seen from almost no other source in the fleet — the Chisel reverse-SOCKS tunnel to the report's endpoint. The ABIOC fires on cadence plus destination rarity; Unit 42 enrichment of the destination then names CL-STA-1178.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter log_source_type = "eal" and action = "allow"
| filter url_domain = dst
| comp count() as recurring_sessions by endpoint_device_name, src, dst
| windowcomp count_distinct(src) as fleet_src_prevalence by dst
| filter recurring_sessions >= 6 and fleet_src_prevalence <= 2
| fields endpoint_device_name, src, dst, recurring_sessions, fleet_src_prevalence
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned host egress baseline -> recurring sessions to a fleet-rare IP-literal destination from the endpoint_device_name that wrote Blackwood.dll.conf.

xql_queries.name: MP-025 Coding-Test Lure Extracted into source/repos

threat_scenarios.name: Blinder Tunnel — Developer Lure to GitHub C2 and Chisel Tunnel, One Incident
threat_scenarios.description: The developer-lure endpoint lineage, the GitHub-as-C2 cadence and the Chisel tunnel / WildFire verdicts land as one Cortex incident on the shared run host, with the published Unit 42 indicators enriching the network leg.

threat_steps.objective: Endpoint lineage alerts fire on the run host: design-time build drops and runs RuntimeBroker.exe, the AppDomainManager/ETW config and the MicrosoftRuntime autostart.
preconditions: XDR agent on the run host.
The project is opened (design-time build) by the developer identity.
steps: Inspect the causality chain from the IDE / build engine to RuntimeBroker.exe.
success_criteria: The build-engine, renamed-host, config and autostart BIOCs fire for the same agent_hostname.

threat_steps.objective: The GitHub cadence ABIOC and the tunnel / WildFire NGFW alerts fire for the same host, enriched by Unit 42.
preconditions: Collector wired to XSIAM as the NGFW source.
steps: Search the tenant for the report indicators.
success_criteria: The tunnel endpoint and the Blackwood hashes resolve to Unit 42 / CL-STA-1178 context.
The report phishing domains are flagged by DNS Security.

threat_steps.objective: CR-MP-0025 stitches the endpoint and network legs into one incident on src_host.
preconditions: TS-MP-025A and TS-MP-025B produced alerts within 900 s.
steps: Open the incident for the run host.
success_criteria: Exactly one incident holds EDR and NDR alerts for the run host.

preventive_controls: Treat third-party Visual Studio projects as untrusted code: open them in a disposable VM, or with design-time builds and project trust prompts enforced, because opening is enough to execute a target.
Block execution from %LOCALAPPDATA% subfolders that impersonate Windows binaries (RuntimeBroker.exe outside System32) with application control.
Restrict GitHub API access from non-developer endpoints and require SaaS inline policy on personal-token API use.
Egress-filter long-lived HTTP sessions to IP-literal destinations; block WebSocket upgrades from non-browser processes.
detection_engineering: Alert on build engines (MSBuild, dotnet) creating and executing binaries outside the build output tree.
Alert on .exe.config files declaring appDomainManagerAssembly or etwEnable=false next to user-writable executables.
Correlate fixed-cadence GitHub API sessions seen at the firewall with the endpoint process lineage on the same host rather than treating GitHub traffic as benign.
